subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Laura — attaching v1 pricing bands + tier→shape mapping for Dedicated (Standard/Plus/Premium). This is what we want to socialize with Sales Enablement next week.

Asks:
- Confirm GM targets / pricing floors by tier (and any must-have guardrails)
- Confirm discount exception process (thresholds + who approves)
- Any concerns with headroom assumptions embedded in the bands

Attachment:
- Dedicated_Tier_Pricing_Bands_v1.xlsx

Notes:
- Bands are per-region (US/EU) but we kept deltas small; supply constraints flagged as “risk” not in list price.
- Premium assumes warm pool + higher spare ratio.

Thanks,
Lauren

—

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 11:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Thanks — reviewed. High level: directionally fine, but we need to tighten the floors + be explicit about discount exceptions.

What Finance needs to be true for GA launch:

1) GM targets (at steady-state utilization):
- Standard: >= 52% blended GM
- Plus: >= 58% blended GM
- Premium: >= 62% blended GM

2) Pricing floors (non-negotiable without exception):
- Any deal that projects <50% GM (post-discount) requires exception approval.
- Any deal using Premium entitlements (warm pool / higher spare ratio) cannot be priced on Standard/Plus bands.

3) Key risks I see in the sheet:
- A100 shapes in EU are priced too close to US while our effective COGS is higher (procurement + lower expected utilization). If we keep the list price flat, we need to cap discounting more aggressively in EU.
- Plus tier “burst included” assumption: if Sales positions burst as “free sustained uplift,” the unit economics break quickly.

Can you add an “operational assumptions” tab that Sales Enablement can’t miss (utilization target, headroom target, burst definition, support allocation)?

Also flagging: I don’t want us promising “Premium” before we have consistent supply by region. Pricing can exist, but availability messaging must be tight.

Laura Bennett
Finance
Redwood Inference

—

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 1:42 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Adding a few numbers from the model runs this morning.

If we assume:
- Standard: 65% utilization target, 15% headroom
- Plus: 62% utilization target, 18% headroom (due to burst reserve)
- Premium: 58% utilization target, 25% headroom (warm pool + spares)

Then the current bands in the spreadsheet yield (pre-discount) GM roughly:
- Standard: 53–56% (OK)
- Plus: 56–59% (low end misses target once we allocate support + control plane)
- Premium: 60–63% (OK in US; EU variants dip below 62% in a couple of shapes)

Two suggestions:
1) Raise Plus list by ~6–8% on the “most common” shapes (we can keep edge shapes the same so we don’t blow up quoting). This is the simplest way to avoid Plus being a discount vehicle.
2) Set discount guardrails explicitly by tier:
- Standard: up to 15% discretionary discount
- Plus: up to 10% discretionary discount
- Premium: up to 5% discretionary discount
Anything beyond that = exception.

Attaching a quick sensitivity PDF with the deltas by tier/region.

Attachment:
- Dedicated_Unit_Econ_Sensitivity_Mar2025.pdf

Rishi

—

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Mar 2, 2025 at 10:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Super helpful.

A couple clarifications so we implement this cleanly:

1) Discount exception process: is the approval chain Deal Desk → Finance (you) → (if below 45% GM) leadership? Or do you want all <50% GM to require leadership?

2) EU pricing: would you prefer we set EU list prices higher than US (simple) OR keep lists flat and cap discounting in EU (messaging pain)?

3) Plus burst: our draft entitlement language is “burst up to X for Y minutes within rolling hour; sustained above commit is billed as burst.” We can tighten Sales enablement copy so it’s clearly not free sustained.

I can update the sheet today with:
- Plus +6–8% on top shapes
- EU adjustment (pending your call)
- Add the “operational assumptions” tab called out

Lauren

—

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 9:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Answers inline.

1) Discount exception process
- Within guardrails (Standard ≤15%, Plus ≤10%, Premium ≤5%): Sales leadership can approve; Finance does not need to be in the loop.
- Outside guardrails OR projected GM <50%: requires Finance approval (me) + documented rationale (competitive, strategic logo, term length, etc.).
- Projected GM <45% OR any bespoke entitlement change (e.g., “Premium warm pool” sold as Plus): requires leadership approval. (We can route that through Neha’s staff meeting; keep volume low.)

2) EU pricing
Prefer higher EU list prices for shapes where COGS is structurally higher. It is easier operationally than policing discounting by region, and it avoids us “discovering” bad GM after the first few EU deals.

3) Plus burst
Agree on tightening language. Please make sure the enablement materials include:
- “Burst is for temporary spikes; sustained throughput above commit is metered as burst (and may be throttled if burst pool is saturated).”
- Explicit examples (one with short spike OK, one with sustained overage billed/denied).

One more thing: please add a single slide/table that maps tier → margin expectation → discount guardrails → exception approvers. Sales needs one place to look.

Laura

—

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 4:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated tiers — pricing bands + GM targets (Finance review)

Got it.

Plan:
- Update pricing bands with EU list uplift for the affected shapes (and call out rationale in notes)
- Increase Plus list on top shapes by 7% (split the difference)
- Add “operational assumptions” tab (utilization/headroom/support allocation + burst definition)
- Add the one-page approver matrix (tier → GM target → discount guardrails → exceptions)

I’ll re-send the updated xlsx tomorrow morning and then we’ll incorporate into the enablement doc tied to PM-497.

Thanks,
Lauren
